`abstract class ElasticTweenEquation`<br/>
**Extends:** [`TweenEquation`](/reference/animation/tweenequation/)<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.animation.tween.equation` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [ElasticTweenEquation.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/animation/tween/equation/ElasticTweenEquation.java)

Easing curves that oscillate like a spring at the start or at the end.

![The Elastic easing curves in a white frame that marks 0 and 1: IN in grey, OUT in dark grey, INOUT in white, with one dot per curve that runs along it from the start to the end](/captures/catalog-easing-elastictweenequation.webp)

## Description

Each constant is also in [`TweenEquations`](/reference/animation/tweenequations/), as `ELASTIC_IN`, `ELASTIC_OUT` and `ELASTIC_IN_OUT`.
`period(...)` and `amplitude(...)` give the same curve with other oscillations, whose `toString()` carries them, period first: `"Elastic.IN(0.3, 2.0)"`, which [`TweenEquations.of`](/reference/animation/tweenequations/#TweenEquations-method-of) reads back.

## Property details

<a id="ElasticTweenEquation-property-period"></a>

### period

- `this period(float period)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>
- `float getPeriod()` 

**Default:** 

The length of one oscillation, as a part of the step: smaller values oscillate faster.
`period(float)` returns a curve of the same direction with that period and leaves this one unchanged.

<a id="ElasticTweenEquation-property-amplitude"></a>

### amplitude

- `this amplitude(float amplitude)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>

**Default:** 

The height of the oscillations; a value below `1F` counts as `1F`.
`amplitude(float)` returns a curve of the same direction with that amplitude and leaves this one unchanged.
